blocks.value: Stock prices move up and down every day, making charts look noisy. A Moving Average smooths these movements and helps us see the overall trend more clearly.

Imagine This: Standing on a beach, individual waves constantly move up and down. But if you watch the sea from far away, you notice its overall direction. A Moving Average works the same way by smoothing daily price fluctuations.
A Moving Average is calculated by taking the average closing price over a selected number of periods, such as 20 days or 50 days.
A 20-Day Moving Average represents the average closing price of the last 20 trading days and updates every new trading day.
Moving Averages help identify trends—they do not predict future prices.
Commonly used Moving Averages include the 20-Day, 50-Day, 100-Day and 200-Day Moving Average.

blocks.question: Why do traders use Moving Averages?
choices: To identify the overall trend more clearly.

blocks.question: A Moving Average is based on...
choices: Average prices over a selected period.
